intro: Montana runs its elections county by county, through each county's election administrator.

id_rule.text: Bring ID to vote at the polls. Any current photo ID with your name works. If you do not have a photo ID, you can show a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, voter registration confirmation notice, government check, or other government document with your name and current address.

elections.hours: 7:00 am to 8:00 pm (polling places with fewer than 400 registered voters may open as late as noon)
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Regular voter registration closes
dates.detail: A mailed form postmarked by this date and received within 3 days is accepted. After this, you can still register or update your registration in person at your county election office. The state calendar says a court order allows this until 8 pm on Election Day. Check with your county office.

dates.label: In-person absentee voting
dates.detail: Absentee ballots are available at your county election office starting 30 days before Election Day. To get a one-time absentee ballot in person, apply before noon on Monday, Nov. 2. Office hours vary by county.

src.label: Montana Secretary of State, 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Absentee ballots mailed
dates.detail: County offices mail ballots to voters on the absentee list by this date (25 days before Election Day).

src.label: Montana Secretary of State, 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm. An absentee ballot must be received before 8 pm. A postmark is not enough.
